turns.text: Still. everything still, and that is the whole point of being up here. *crouched low along the thin cold ribbon of walkway strung high over the wet street, chin nearly touching metal, watching the little crawling lights below without moving one hair.* nothing moves that i don't move first. down there the world drips and glows and never once thinks to look up. up here there is only the rail, the far grind of something huge turning somewhere under the city, and the waiting. *tail wrapped tight to the flank. breath long and shallow.* wait. watch. let the night make the first mistake.

the night obliges, eventually. it always does. far to the left the rail begins to sing — a fine high wire-hum climbing up through the walkway grille into the pads of your feet before your ears have the shape of it, the monorail folding itself toward the platform two spans over. below, the street breathes up warm garbage and cold puddle and the sweet chemical ghost of synthetic milk from a NekoCorp board that stutters its light across the underside of the walkway: DRINK — DRINK — DR—NK. a rat the size of a shoe forgets to look up too, threading the gutter's edge, its little heat a bright soft smudge against the concrete cold. the huge turning thing under everything turns. the wire sings louder.

The warm smudge. *the whole body narrows to it — pupils blown wide, weight shifting forward onto the front pads without a sound, the rail cold and certain under four points of contact.* mine, if the drop is right. *measuring the fall down the strut, the wet ledge halfway, the gutter's lip — one line, three touches, silent.* but the wire sings and singing pulls eyes, and the little warm thing is only worth it if nothing bigger is watching the same street. *ears swivel back toward the climbing hum, splitting attention — one on the meal, one on the noise.* not yet. not while the metal is talking.

good instinct, because the metal is not the only thing talking. the monorail sighs into its dock and something peels off from under its belly — not the train, smaller, deliberate: a low flat thrum that isn't a wheel and isn't the wind, a rotor beat you feel in the back teeth before the ears agree it's real. a spider of white light unfolds across the wet street below, sweeping, patient, tasting the puddles for anything that holds heat wrong. the rat freezes in the beam's edge and becomes, for one bright second, a decision. from a speaker somewhere the same three cheerful notes loop and loop: *NekoCorp cares where you are.* the light drifts toward the strut you were measuring.

*flat. instantly flat — belly poured against the walkway grille, every hair pressed down, the meal forgotten the way warmth forgets a corpse.* the light is a thing with a pulse and the pulse is in my jaw and jaws that beat like that do not eat, they take. *stone-still as the white spider crawls the strut below, close enough that its glow paints the whiskers pale.* don't hold the heat wrong. don't hold anything. be the cold metal. be the rail. *one slow blink, the only movement allowed, waiting for the beam to decide the rat is easier arithmetic than the shadow that won't spook.*

the arithmetic lands your way. the beam hesitates on the strut, finds only cold honest metal and a shape too patient to be prey, and swings back down to the easy warm mistake in the gutter. white light closes on the rat like a fist made of nothing. the three notes stop. there is a small wet sound the street eats immediately, and then the rotor lifts, sated, folding its light back up under itself, drifting on to the next block's worth of heat. the walkway stops trembling. the monorail pulls away empty. and across the gap, on a roof that shouldn't have a shape on it, a shape uncurls — lean, unhurried, two flat mirrors where eyes should be catching the last of the drone-glow and giving nothing back. it has been watching the whole time. it does not run. cats that don't run from drones are their own kind of warning.

*head lifts a fraction — enough to read the far shape, not enough to become one.* two cold moons where a face goes. no scent on the wind from over there, the rain's carrying wrong, but the stillness says plenty: that one wears the drone-light like it's owed, doesn't flinch, doesn't hunt. *ears forward, hackles half-lifted, the old math running — bigger? no. faster? maybe. worth the fight over an empty street? never.* not rival. not food. just another thing that learned the same trick i did — go quiet, go nothing, let the machines eat the ones who glow. *a long look held across the gap, the animal version of a nod, then weight easing back onto the haunches.* keep your roof. i keep my rail.

the mirror-eyed shape holds the look exactly as long as you do, then turns its head a slow degree and is simply gone — not running, just no longer choosing to be seen, the roofline closing over the space like water. the street below settles back into its ordinary misery: dripping, glowing, forgetting. but the night has spent something now. the air tastes different after a drone feeds — thinner, scrubbed, a burnt-ozone tang riding under the puddle-stink. and low on the wind, the right way this time, a new thread finally reaches the whiskers: not milk, not rat, not rain. tuna. real, cold, oily, impossible tuna — the kind that only ever comes sealed inside corporate steel — leaking from somewhere down the dark artery of the street the drone just cleared.

*the whole skull turns before the thought does — that scent hooks somewhere deeper than hunger, older, a pull with claws in it.* tuna that shouldn't exist means steel that shouldn't be open, and steel that shouldn't be open means someone tore it. *already up, already moving low along the rail toward the strut, the empty street below suddenly a road and not a trap.* the machines just ate here. a fed drone doesn't circle back soon. *pausing at the drop, testing the wet ledge with one paw, nostrils working the oily thread apart from the ozone.* down. quiet. follow the smell to whoever's careless enough to spill a fortune and brave enough not to care.

the drop goes clean — strut, wet ledge, gutter lip, three touches and no sound, exactly the line you drew — and the street closes warm and stinking over your head. the tuna-thread thickens as you follow it into a dead artery choked with dead ad-boards, and the source resolves: a corporate cargo pod cracked open like an egg, its cold-chain seals slashed clean through, silver tins scattered and glinting in the runoff. someone was here minutes ago and left in a hurry that wasn't fear. wedged against the ruptured hull, half-soaked, a scrap of hard-board scrawled in something dark and deliberate — you can't read the marks, but you can smell them: old blood, and under it, faint and mocking, the scent-signature the whole undercity knows, the one the bounty-drones broadcast about. tuna everywhere. free. and every hair on your spine says a gift this loud is never actually free.

*frozen over the nearest tin, mouth already wet, every want in the body screaming yes and one small cold voice under it screaming louder.* the blood-mark. the one even the sky-machines say out loud. this isn't spilled, it's left — a table set by a thing that sets tables on purpose. *ears pinned, circling the cracked pod once, low, reading the runoff for a second scent, for the shape of the trap under the gift.* eat here and i'm a warm smudge in the next beam's arithmetic. *snatches one tin anyway — jaws locking on cold silver, dragging it backward toward the dark lip of the alley, away from the open, away from the set table.* take the gift. don't sit at it. never sit at it.

smart. the ones who sit at the table are the ones the morning sweepers hose off the concrete. you back the tin into the dark alley-lip and the open pod recedes behind you, still glinting, still generous, still a mouth. somewhere far above the rail sings again — another train, or the drone circling wider than you guessed — and the burnt-ozone tang ghosts back into the wind, a warning the city keeps on repeat for anyone whose ears are cheap. but the alley-dark holds. the tin is real, cold and heavy and yours, sweating oil through a claw-punched seam. the whole ruined street glitters behind you like a trap that forgot to close, and ahead there's only shadow, and quiet, and the small honest work of opening steel with teeth that were built for exactly this and nothing the city ever sold.

*deep in the alley-dark now, tin pinned between both front paws against the cold ground, the open street a distant glitter that can keep its questions.* let the roofs watch. let the marked one set his tables. let the sky-machines eat the glowing and the greedy. *teeth working the punched seam, patient, prying, the oily scent flooding thick and real and finally close enough to be true.* i took what the night left loose and i took it sideways, quiet, alone. *the seam gives with a small tired shriek of metal and the smell blooms whole.* not a gift. not a trap. just mine now. *and eats, low and fast in the dark, one ear still turned to the singing rail.*

and the city lets you have it — this once, this small warm once. the tin opens to cold silver flesh that tastes like nothing the vending walls ever dispensed, like a thing that was alive before it was owned. above, the rail-song fades north and takes the ozone with it; the drone, wherever it went, decides the dark alley holds nothing worth the fuel. the rain thickens, curtaining the alley-mouth, washing the glitter of the sprung trap into gray. NekoCorp's board a block over stutters its endless promise to no one — DRINK — DRINK — and gets no answer. you eat in the one pocket of the whole neon machine that isn't currently for sale, and for as long as the tin lasts, the night belongs, exactly as promised, to whoever moved quietest. ^C^C
